T: Find out how you like your eggs.
D: A newspaper columnist heads to a small Maryland town to write about a woman who keeps leaving men at the altar.
P: Serve the mains when Maggie finally works out how she likes her eggs.
S: Maggie's family hardware store in Hale

Popcorn coated in a buttery brown sugar caramel, baked crunchy, salted and scooped into brown paper bags like a shop counter treat. Pop 100g popcorn kernels in 2 tbsp oil in a lidded pot and tip into a large roasting tin. Boil 100g butter, 200g brown sugar, 60ml golden syrup and half a teaspoon salt for 4 minutes, then stir in half a teaspoon bicarb so it foams. Pour over the popcorn and toss. Bake at 120C for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, then spread out to cool. Sprinkle with flaky salt and scoop into paper bags.
Crab cakes with mayo, Dijon and spring onion, pan fried
Crab meat bound with mayo, mustard, spring onion and breadcrumbs, shaped into small cakes and pan-fried until golden, with lemon.
Grated potato and onion cakes fried in butter
Grated potato and onion squeezed dry, fried in butter in small cakes until crisp, served with sour cream and chives.
M: Poached eggs and hollandaise on toasted English muffins
Eggs poached 3 minutes, set on toasted English muffins with ham, covered in hollandaise of yolks whisked with melted butter and lemon.
yet another rehearsal dinner for Maggie

Chicken rubbed with butter, lemon and thyme, roasted at 200C for 75 minutes, with roast potatoes and a pan gravy. Rub a 1.8kg chicken with 40g soft butter, lemon zest, thyme and salt and put the halved lemon inside. Roast at 200C for 75 minutes. Parboil 1kg potatoes in chunks for 8 minutes, rough them up and roast in hot oil alongside for 50 minutes. Rest the chicken 10 minutes. Stir 1 tbsp plain flour into the pan juices, whisk in 300ml chicken stock and simmer into gravy. Carve and serve with the potatoes and gravy.
W: Butter sponge layers with strawberry jam and whipped cream
Two vanilla sponges baked at 175C for 25 minutes, sandwiched with strawberry jam and whipped cream, iced white.
K: Orange juice and zest blended with vanilla ice cream, milk and honey

Fresh orange juice blended with vanilla ice cream, cold milk and orange zest into a creamy old-school diner shake. Squeeze 4 oranges to get about 300ml juice and zest one of them. Blend the juice and zest with 6 scoops vanilla ice cream, 200ml cold milk and 1 tbsp honey until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 tall glasses and finish each with a thin orange slice on the rim and a straw.

note.text: Everyone in town has a story about me and the church doors. I'm still working out what kind of eggs I like.

ingredients.item: cans hearts of palm (400 g each), drained

steps.text: Chop the hearts of palm finely and squeeze dry in a clean tea towel.
Mix with the nori, mayonnaise, Dijon, sliced spring onion and breadcrumbs.
Shape into small cakes and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Pan-fry in the oil until golden on both sides.
Serve with lemon wedges.

Season and shape into small flat cakes.
Fry in butter over medium heat until crisp on both sides.

dishes.make_ahead: Hollandaise is best fresh, keep warm up to 30 minutes

Whisk the 3 yolks with lemon juice over a gentle simmer, then slowly pour in the butter until thick.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water.
Toast the muffins and top with ham and the eggs.
Spoon over the hollandaise and finish with chives.

ingredients.item: eggs (3 yolks for the sauce, 8 for poaching)

steps.text: Melt 150 g of the butter.
Whisk the 3 yolks with lemon juice over a gentle simmer, then slowly pour in the melted butter until thick.
Fry the mushrooms in the rest of the butter, then wilt the spinach in the same pan.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water and toast the muffins.
Top the muffins with spinach, mushrooms and eggs, spoon over the hollandaise and finish with chives.

Bake at 175C until golden and springy.
Cool completely.
Whip the cream and sandwich the cakes with jam and cream.
Ice white with icing sugar mixed with milk.

s.note: Crab cakes with mayo, Dijon and spring onion, pan fried
s.how: Mix 400g crab meat with 2 tbsp mayonnaise, a spoon of Dijon, sliced spring onion and half a cup of breadcrumbs. Shape into small cakes and chill 30 minutes. Pan-fry until golden on both sides and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Grated potato and onion cakes fried in butter
s.how: Grate 800g potatoes and a small onion, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can. Season and shape into small flat cakes. Fry in butter over medium heat for 5 minutes a side until crisp. Serve hot with sour cream and chives.

m.note: Poached eggs and hollandaise on toasted English muffins
m.how: Melt 150g butter. Whisk 3 yolks with lemon juice over a gentle simmer, then slowly pour in the butter until thick. Poach 8 eggs for 3 minutes. Toast 4 English muffins, top with ham and the eggs and spoon over the hollandaise. Finish with chives.

w.note: Butter sponge layers with strawberry jam and whipped cream
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Sandwich with strawberry jam and whipped cream and ice white. Keep a running start in case the bride bolts.

d.note: Orange juice and zest blended with vanilla ice cream, milk and honey
d.how: Squeeze 4 oranges to get about 300ml juice and zest one of them. Blend the juice and zest with 6 scoops vanilla ice cream, 200ml cold milk and 1 tbsp honey until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 tall glasses and finish each with a thin orange slice on the rim and a straw.
